source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ חָנ֥וּן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after thus, and died [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon, and reigned Hanun his son in his place.

en.L: And it happened after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Some time after this, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king in his place.
en.R: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became the new king.

es.L: Y sucedió después de esto que murió el rey de los hijos de Amón, y reinó en su lugar Hanún su hijo.
es.B: Algún tiempo después, murió el rey de los amonitas, y su hijo Hanún reinó en su lugar.
es.R: Algún tiempo después, el rey de los amonitas murió, y su hijo Hanún llegó a ser el nuevo rey.

fr.L: Et il arriva après cela que le roi des fils d’Ammon mourut, et Hanoun son fils régna à sa place.
fr.B: Quelque temps après, le roi des Ammonites mourut, et son fils Hanoun devint roi à sa place.
fr.R: Quelque temps plus tard, le roi des Ammonites est mort, et son fils Hanoun est devenu le nouveau roi.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya hayo mfalme wa wana wa Amoni akafa, naye Hanuni mwanawe akatawala mahali pake.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo, mfalme wa Waamoni alikufa, na mwanawe Hanuni akawa mfalme mahali pake.
sw.R: Baadaye mfalme wa Waamoni alikufa, na mwanawe Hanuni akawa mfalme mpya.

vi.L: Sau việc này, vua của con cháu Am-môn qua đời, và Ha-nun con trai vua lên trị vì thay cho cha.
vi.B: Sau đó ít lâu, vua của người Am-môn qua đời, và con trai vua là Ha-nun lên ngôi thay cho cha.
vi.R: Một thời gian sau, vua của người Am-môn qua đời, và con trai vua là Ha-nun lên làm vua mới.

ko.L: 그리고 그 뒤에 암몬 자손의 왕이 죽고, 그의 아들 하눈이 그를 대신하여 왕이 되었다.
ko.B: 얼마 뒤에 암몬 사람들의 왕이 죽고, 그의 아들 하눈이 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.
ko.R: 얼마 뒤에 암몬 사람들의 왕이 죽고, 그의 아들 하눈이 새 왕이 되었다.

decisions.choice: after this: a loose link to what comes before, not a date
decisions.reason: The phrase opens a new story without saying how long after the events of chapters 8 and 9 it happened. Chapter 8 has already listed David's victories over Aram and Ammon in brief (8:3-12); this chapter and the next tell how the war with Ammon and its Aramean allies began and was fought.

decisions.choice: the king of the Ammonites: Nahash, named in the next verse
decisions.reason: Ammon was a kingdom east of the Jordan, with its capital at Rabbah (11:1; 12:26). Its king Nahash had besieged Jabesh-gilead in the days of Saul (1 Samuel 11:1-11; 12:12).

decisions.choice: the sons of Ammon (Literal); the Ammonites (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Ammon" is the usual Hebrew name for the people of Ammon. Literal keeps the phrase; Balanced and Readable use the people's name, as throughout this chapter.

decisions.choice: les fils d'Ammon (L); les Ammonites (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the Hebrew name of the people; Balanced and Readable use the usual French name, as the Samuel terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Amón" (L); "los amonitas" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English levels and the Samuel terms note: Literal keeps the Hebrew name of the people, and Balanced and Readable say "los amonitas", for the whole of 2 Samuel.

decisions.choice: wana wa Amoni (Literal); Waamoni (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name "sons of Ammon"; Balanced and Readable use the people's name, Waamoni, throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Am-môn" (L); "người Am-môn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps "sons of Ammon", the other levels name the people; the names "Ha-nun", "Na-hách", "Bết-Rê-hóp", "Tóp", "Hê-lam" and "Sô-bác" in this chapter take the usual Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "암몬 자손" (L); "암몬 사람들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "sons of Ammon"; Korean "자손" includes the whole people, so no gender span is needed.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶעֱשֶׂה־חֶ֣סֶד׀עִם־חָנ֣וּן בֶּן־נָחָ֗שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂ֨ה אָבִ֤יו עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח דָּוִ֧ד לְנַחֲמ֛וֹ בְּיַד־עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶל־אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, I will do chesed with Hanun son of Nahash just as did his father with me chesed; and sent David to comfort him by [the] hand of his servants concerning his father; and came [the] servants of David [to the] land of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And David said, "I will deal [in] steadfast love with Hanun the son of Nahash, just as his father dealt [in] steadfast love with me." So David sent to comfort him by [the] hand of his servants concerning his father. And David's servants came [into the] land of the sons of Ammon.
en.B: David said, "I will show faithful love to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed faithful love to me." So David sent his officials to console Hanun over the death of his father. And David's officials came to the land of the Ammonites.
en.R: David said, "Hanun's father Nahash showed faithful love to me. So I will show faithful love to his son Hanun." David sent some of his officials to comfort Hanun because his father had died. They went to the land of the Ammonites.

es.L: Y dijo David: «Haré amor leal con Hanún hijo de Nahas, así como su padre hizo amor leal conmigo». Y envió David a consolarlo por medio de sus siervos acerca de su padre. Y llegaron los siervos de David [a la] tierra de los hijos de Amón.
es.B: David dijo: «Mostraré amor fiel a Hanún hijo de Nahas, así como su padre me mostró amor fiel a mí». Así que David envió a sus oficiales para consolar a Hanún por la muerte de su padre. Y los oficiales de David llegaron a la tierra de los amonitas.
es.R: David dijo: «Nahas, el padre de Hanún, me mostró amor fiel. Por eso yo mostraré amor fiel a su hijo Hanún». David envió a algunos de sus oficiales para consolar a Hanún porque su padre había muerto. Ellos fueron a la tierra de los amonitas.

fr.L: Et David dit : « J’agirai avec amour loyal envers Hanoun fils de Nahash, comme son père a agi avec amour loyal envers moi. » Et David envoya, par la main de ses serviteurs, le consoler au sujet de son père. Et les serviteurs de David arrivèrent [au] pays des fils d’Ammon.
fr.B: David dit : « Je montrerai un amour fidèle à Hanoun fils de Nahash, comme son père m’a montré un amour fidèle. » David envoya donc ses officiers consoler Hanoun de la mort de son père. Et les officiers de David arrivèrent au pays des Ammonites.
fr.R: David a dit : « Nahash, le père de Hanoun, m’a montré un amour fidèle. Alors je vais montrer un amour fidèle à son fils Hanoun. » David a envoyé quelques-uns de ses officiers pour consoler Hanoun de la mort de son père. Ils sont allés au pays des Ammonites.

sw.L: Daudi akasema, "Nitamtendea Hanuni mwana wa Nahashi upendo usiokoma, kama baba yake alivyonitendea upendo usiokoma." Basi Daudi akatuma kumfariji kwa mkono wa watumishi wake kuhusu baba yake. Watumishi wa Daudi wakafika [katika] nchi ya wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: Daudi akasema, "Nitamtendea Hanuni mwana wa Nahashi fadhili, kama baba yake alivyonitendea fadhili." Basi Daudi alituma maafisa wake kumfariji Hanuni kwa kifo cha baba yake. Maafisa wa Daudi wakafika katika nchi ya Waamoni.
sw.R: Daudi akasema, "Nahashi baba yake Hanuni alinitendea fadhili. Basi nami nitamtendea fadhili mwanawe Hanuni." Daudi akatuma baadhi ya maafisa wake kumfariji Hanuni kwa sababu baba yake amekufa. Wakaenda katika nchi ya Waamoni.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói: "Ta sẽ tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín với Ha-nun con trai Na-hách, như cha người đã tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín với ta." Vậy Đa-vít sai các đầy tớ mình đi an ủi người về việc cha người qua đời. Các đầy tớ của Đa-vít đến xứ của con cháu Am-môn.
vi.B: Đa-vít nói: "Ta sẽ tỏ lòng nhân từ với Ha-nun con trai Na-hách, như cha người đã tỏ lòng nhân từ với ta." Vậy Đa-vít sai các quần thần đi chia buồn với Ha-nun về cái chết của cha người. Các quần thần của Đa-vít đến xứ của người Am-môn.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói: "Na-hách, cha của Ha-nun, đã tỏ lòng nhân từ với ta. Vậy ta sẽ tỏ lòng nhân từ với Ha-nun con trai người." Đa-vít sai một số quần thần đi chia buồn với Ha-nun vì cha người đã qua đời. Họ đến xứ của người Am-môn.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 말했다. "하눈의 아버지가 나에게 한결같은 사랑을 베풀었던 것처럼, 내가 나하스의 아들 하눈에게 한결같은 사랑을 베풀겠다." 그래서 다윗이 그의 아버지 일로 그를 위로하려고 자기 신하들의 손을 [빌려 사람을] 보냈다. 그리고 다윗의 신하들이 암몬 자손의 땅에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 다윗이 말했다. "하눈의 아버지 나하스가 나에게 인애를 베풀었으니, 나도 그의 아들 하눈에게 인애를 베풀겠다." 그래서 다윗은 하눈이 아버지를 잃은 것을 위로하려고 신하들을 보냈다. 다윗의 신하들이 암몬 사람들의 땅에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 다윗이 말했다. "하눈의 아버지 나하스는 나에게 인애를 보여 주었다. 그러니 나도 그의 아들 하눈에게 인애를 보여 주겠다." 다윗은 하눈의 아버지가 죽었기 때문에 그를 위로하려고 신하 몇 사람을 보냈다. 그들은 암몬 사람들의 땅으로 갔다.

decisions.choice: chesed: loyal kindness between allies
decisions.reason: Chesed is love that keeps faith within a bond (1 Samuel 20:8). Between two kings it is the loyalty of friends or treaty partners: Nahash had been good to David, and David means to keep up the friendship with his son. The same word is used of God's own love (Exodus 34:6).

decisions.choice: as his father showed to me: a kindness the books of Samuel do not describe
decisions.reason: The text never says what Nahash had done for David. Nahash had been Saul's enemy (1 Samuel 11), so he may have helped David while Saul was hunting him. Later, when David fled from Absalom, Shobi son of Nahash of Rabbah brought him supplies (17:27).

decisions.choice: I will show chesed: David's words echo the chapter before
decisions.reason: In 9:1, 3 and 7 David asked whether anyone was left of Saul's house to whom he could show chesed, and he showed it to Mephibosheth. Here he offers the same loyalty to Hanun, and it is rejected.

decisions.choice: sent to comfort him concerning his father: a formal embassy of condolence
decisions.reason: When a king died, friendly rulers sent envoys to mourn with his heir. Such a visit also confirmed that the friendship between the two kingdoms would go on under the new king.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is rendered the same way throughout, as in Exodus 34:6 and 1 Samuel 20:8.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The servants of a king are his officials, here sent as envoys. Literal keeps "servants"; Balanced and Readable say "officials", as elsewhere in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "Hanún hijo de Nahas"
decisions.reason: Names in their usual Spanish forms, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương thành tín" (L); "lòng nhân từ" (B, R) for *chesed* between allies
decisions.reason: Loyal kindness between allies (meaning decision), in the forms set at 2:5 for *ḥesed* between people.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל־חָנ֣וּן אֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֗ם הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַֽחֲמִ֑ים הֲ֠לוֹא בַּעֲב֞וּר חֲק֤וֹר אֶת־הָעִיר֙ וּלְרַגְּלָ֣הּ וּלְהָפְכָ֔הּ שָׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] princes of [the] sons of Ammon to Hanun their lord, [Is] honoring David your father in your eyes because he has sent to you comforters? [Is it] not in order to search the city and to spy it out and to overthrow it [that] has sent David his servants to you?

en.L: And the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Is David honoring your father in your eyes because he has sent comforters to you? Is it not in order to search the city and to spy it out and to overthrow it that David has sent his servants to you?"
en.B: But the Ammonite officials said to Hanun their lord, "Do you really think David is honoring your father by sending men to comfort you? Has David not sent his officials to you to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?"
en.R: But the leaders of the Ammonites said to Hanun, their master, "Do you really believe David sent these men to comfort you because he respects your father? No! David sent them to look over the city and spy on it, so that he can capture it."

es.L: Y dijeron los príncipes de los hijos de Amón a Hanún su señor: «¿Honra David a tu padre a tus ojos porque te ha enviado consoladores? ¿No es para explorar la ciudad y para espiarla y para destruirla que David te ha enviado a sus siervos?».
es.B: Pero los oficiales amonitas le dijeron a Hanún, su señor: «¿De veras crees que David honra a tu padre al enviarte hombres para consolarte? ¿No te ha enviado David a sus oficiales para explorar la ciudad, espiarla y destruirla?».
es.R: Pero los líderes de los amonitas le dijeron a Hanún, su señor: «¿De veras crees que David envió a estos hombres a consolarte porque respeta a tu padre? ¡No! David los envió a recorrer la ciudad y espiarla, para poder conquistarla».

fr.L: Et les princes des fils d’Ammon dirent à Hanoun leur seigneur : « Est-ce pour honorer ton père, à tes yeux, que David t’a envoyé des consolateurs ? N’est-ce pas pour explorer la ville, et pour l’espionner, et pour la renverser, que David t’a envoyé ses serviteurs ? »
fr.B: Mais les chefs ammonites dirent à Hanoun, leur seigneur : « Crois-tu vraiment que David veuille honorer ton père en t’envoyant des gens pour te consoler ? N’est-ce pas plutôt pour explorer la ville, l’espionner et la détruire que David t’a envoyé ses officiers ? »
fr.R: Mais les chefs des Ammonites ont dit à Hanoun, leur maître : « Tu crois vraiment que David t’a envoyé ces hommes pour te consoler parce qu’il respecte ton père ? Non ! David les a envoyés pour observer la ville et l’espionner, afin de pouvoir s’en emparer. »

sw.L: Wakuu wa wana wa Amoni wakamwambia Hanuni bwana wao, "Je, Daudi anamheshimu baba yako machoni pako kwa kuwa amekutumia wafariji? Je, Daudi hakuwatuma watumishi wake kwako ili kuupeleleza mji na kuuchunguza na kuuangamiza?"
sw.B: Lakini maafisa wa Waamoni wakamwambia Hanuni bwana wao, "Je, kweli unadhani Daudi anamheshimu baba yako kwa kukutumia watu wa kukufariji? Je, Daudi hakuwatuma maafisa wake kwako ili wauchunguze mji, waupeleleze, na kuuangamiza?"
sw.R: Lakini viongozi wa Waamoni wakamwambia Hanuni bwana wao, "Je, kweli unaamini kwamba Daudi amewatuma watu hawa kukufariji kwa sababu anamheshimu baba yako? Hapana! Daudi amewatuma kuukagua mji na kuupeleleza, ili apate kuuteka."

vi.L: Các thủ lĩnh của con cháu Am-môn nói với Ha-nun, chúa của họ: "Có phải trong mắt bệ hạ, Đa-vít tôn kính cha bệ hạ vì hắn đã sai người đến an ủi bệ hạ sao? Chẳng phải Đa-vít sai các đầy tớ hắn đến với bệ hạ để dò xét thành, do thám thành và lật đổ thành sao?"
vi.B: Nhưng các quan chức của người Am-môn nói với Ha-nun, chúa của họ: "Bệ hạ thật sự nghĩ rằng Đa-vít tôn kính cha bệ hạ khi sai người đến chia buồn với bệ hạ sao? Chẳng phải Đa-vít sai các quần thần của hắn đến với bệ hạ để dò xét thành, do thám và lật đổ thành sao?"
vi.R: Nhưng các nhà lãnh đạo của người Am-môn nói với Ha-nun, chủ của họ: "Đức vua thật sự tin rằng Đa-vít sai những người này đến chia buồn vì hắn kính trọng cha của đức vua sao? Không đâu! Đa-vít sai họ đến để xem xét và do thám thành này, để hắn chiếm lấy nó."

ko.L: 그리고 암몬 자손의 고관들이 그들의 주 하눈에게 말했다. "다윗이 당신에게 위로하는 자들을 보냈다고 해서, 당신 눈에는 그가 당신의 아버지를 존경하는 것[으로 보입니까]? 다윗이 그 성을 살피고 정탐하여 뒤엎으려고 그의 신하들을 당신에게 보낸 것이 아닙니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 암몬의 고관들이 그들의 주인 하눈에게 말했다. "다윗이 위로하는 사람들을 보냈다고 해서, 정말로 그가 임금님의 아버지를 존경한다고 생각하십니까? 다윗이 이 성을 살피고 정탐해서 무너뜨리려고 신하들을 임금님께 보낸 것이 아니겠습니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 암몬의 지도자들이 그들의 주인 하눈에게 말했다. "다윗이 임금님의 아버지를 존경해서 위로하는 사람들을 보냈다고 정말 믿으십니까? 아닙니다! 다윗은 이 성을 둘러보고 정탐해서 빼앗으려고 그들을 보낸 것입니다."

decisions.choice: is David honoring your father in your eyes?: do you think he is?
decisions.reason: "In your eyes" means "in your opinion". The question expects the answer "no": the officials are telling Hanun not to believe that the visit is a mark of respect.

decisions.choice: is it not in order to ...?: a question that states what they believe
decisions.reason: The second question expects the answer "yes". The officials claim the envoys came as spies.

decisions.choice: search, spy out, overthrow: scout the city in order to take it
decisions.reason: "The city" is Ammon's capital, Rabbah (11:1; 12:26). The three verbs build up from looking it over to destroying it. The fear was not far-fetched, since David had just conquered Moab, Aram and Edom (8:2-14).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word names the chief men around a king. The three levels follow the wording settled for this word in Samuel.

decisions.choice: No! David sent them to ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the second question into the statement it implies, so that young readers do not miss the point.

decisions.choice: les princes (L); les chefs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word names the chief men around a king (*sarim*). Literal keeps "princes"; Balanced and Readable say "chefs", so that "officiers" stays for the king's servants.

decisions.choice: wakuu (Literal); maafisa (Balanced); viongozi (Readable)
decisions.reason: The chief men around a king, following the English levels.

decisions.choice: the Ammonite officials say "bệ hạ" (L, B) and "đức vua" (R) to Hanun and "hắn" of David
decisions.reason: Subjects to their own king, in the Samuel terms note's forms; Literal takes "bệ hạ" too, since "vua" alone would sound as if they spoke of a third king. Their contempt for David shows in "hắn".

decisions.choice: The Ammonite officials call Hanun "임금님" at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps the Hebrew "당신"
decisions.reason: Korean courtiers would address their king by title; "당신" to a king sounds rude in Korean, though the Hebrew has only "you".

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חָנ֜וּן אֶת־עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיְגַלַּח֙ אֶת־חֲצִ֣י זְקָנָ֔ם וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת אֶת־מַדְוֵיהֶ֛ם בַּחֵ֖צִי עַ֣ד שְׁתֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Hanun [the] servants of David and shaved half of their beard, and cut off their garments in the middle as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.

en.L: So Hanun took David's servants and shaved off half of their beard, and cut off their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
en.B: So Hanun seized David's officials, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut off their garments in the middle at their buttocks, and sent them away.
en.R: So Hanun took David's officials and shaved off half of each man's beard. He cut their robes short, so that their backsides were left bare. Then he sent them away.

es.L: Entonces Hanún tomó a los siervos de David y les rapó la mitad de la barba, y les cortó los vestidos por la mitad, hasta las nalgas, y los despidió.
es.B: Así que Hanún apresó a los oficiales de David, le rapó a cada uno la mitad de la barba, les cortó los vestidos por la mitad a la altura de las nalgas y los despidió.
es.R: Así que Hanún tomó a los oficiales de David y le afeitó a cada uno la mitad de la barba. Les cortó la ropa tan corta que les quedaron las nalgas al descubierto. Luego los despidió.

fr.L: Et Hanoun prit les serviteurs de David, et leur rasa la moitié de leur barbe, et coupa leurs vêtements par le milieu jusqu’à leurs fesses, et les renvoya.
fr.B: Hanoun se saisit donc des officiers de David, fit raser à chacun la moitié de la barbe, fit couper leurs vêtements par le milieu, à hauteur des fesses, et les renvoya.
fr.R: Alors Hanoun a fait prendre les officiers de David et il a fait raser la moitié de la barbe de chacun. Il a fait couper leurs robes très court, si bien qu’on voyait leurs fesses. Puis il les a renvoyés.

sw.L: Basi Hanuni akawatwaa watumishi wa Daudi akawanyoa nusu ya ndevu zao, akayakata mavazi yao katikati mpaka matakoni mwao, akawaacha waende.
sw.B: Basi Hanuni aliwakamata maafisa wa Daudi, akamnyoa kila mmoja nusu ya ndevu zake, akayakata mavazi yao katikati hadi matakoni, akawaacha waende.
sw.R: Basi Hanuni akawakamata maafisa wa Daudi, akamnyoa kila mmoja nusu ya ndevu zake. Akayakata mavazi yao mafupi, hata matako yao yakabaki wazi. Kisha akawaacha waende.

vi.L: Vậy Ha-nun bắt các đầy tớ của Đa-vít, cạo một nửa râu của họ, cắt áo họ ở giữa cho đến mông, rồi đuổi họ đi.
vi.B: Vậy Ha-nun bắt các quần thần của Đa-vít, cạo một nửa râu của mỗi người, cắt áo họ ngang giữa cho đến mông, rồi đuổi họ đi.
vi.R: Vậy Ha-nun bắt các quần thần của Đa-vít và cạo một nửa râu của mỗi người. Hắn cắt ngắn áo họ đến nỗi phía sau bị hở mông. Rồi hắn đuổi họ đi.

ko.L: 그래서 하눈이 다윗의 신하들을 붙잡아 그들의 수염 절반을 깎고, 그들의 옷을 엉덩이까지 중간을 잘라 내고, 그들을 돌려보냈다.
ko.B: 그래서 하눈은 다윗의 신하들을 붙잡아 저마다 수염을 반쪽씩 깎고, 그들의 옷을 엉덩이가 드러나도록 중간을 잘라 낸 뒤에 돌려보냈다.
ko.R: 그래서 하눈은 다윗의 신하들을 붙잡아 한 사람 한 사람의 수염을 반쪽만 깎아 버렸다. 그리고 그들의 옷을 짧게 잘라서 엉덩이가 드러나게 했다. 그러고는 그들을 돌려보냈다.

decisions.choice: shaving off half the beard: a deliberate public insult
decisions.reason: A full beard was a mark of a grown man's honor. Men cut their beards only in deep mourning or disgrace (Isaiah 15:2; Jeremiah 41:5; 48:37). Shaving off half of it by force made the envoys look ridiculous, and the insult fell on David, who had sent them.

decisions.choice: cutting their garments to the buttocks: stripping them like captives
decisions.reason: Long robes were the dress of men of standing. Cutting them off at the buttocks left the men exposed, the shame done to prisoners of war (Isaiah 20:4 uses the same word for their bared buttocks). To treat a king's envoys this way was to reject his friendship and amounted to a challenge to war.

decisions.choice: half of their beard: half of each man's beard
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their beard" in the singular, speaking of each man in turn.

decisions.choice: half of each man's beard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "each man's beard" so the sense is clear; Literal keeps the singular "beard".

decisions.choice: He cut their robes short, so that their backsides were left bare
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the cut did, which is the point of the insult.

source.text: וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַד־יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they told David, and he sent to meet them, for were the men humiliated greatly. And said the king, Stay in Jericho until grows your beard, and you will return.

en.L: And they told David, and he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly humiliated. And the king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beard has grown, and [then] return."
en.B: When David was told, he sent messengers to meet them, because the men were deeply ashamed. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then come home."
en.R: When David heard what had happened, he sent people to meet the men, because they were so ashamed. The king told them, "Wait in Jericho until your beards grow again. Then come home."

es.L: Y se lo informaron a David, y él envió a su encuentro, porque los hombres estaban muy avergonzados. Y dijo el rey: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en Jericó hasta que {{plural_you:les|os}} crezca la barba, y [después] {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}}».
es.B: Cuando se lo dijeron a David, él envió mensajeros a su encuentro, porque los hombres estaban muy avergonzados. El rey les dijo: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en Jericó hasta que {{plural_you:les|os}} vuelva a crecer la barba, y después {{plural_you:regresen|regresad}} a casa».
es.R: Cuando David supo lo que había pasado, envió gente a recibir a los hombres, porque estaban muy avergonzados. El rey les dijo: «{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}} en Jericó hasta que {{plural_you:les|os}} crezca otra vez la barba. Después {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a casa».

fr.L: Et on [l’]annonça à David, et il envoya [des gens] à leur rencontre, car les hommes étaient très humiliés. Et le roi dit : « Restez à Jéricho jusqu’à ce que votre barbe ait poussé, et [ensuite] revenez. »
fr.B: Quand on en informa David, il envoya des messagers à leur rencontre, car ces hommes étaient profondément humiliés. Le roi leur fit dire : « Restez à Jéricho jusqu’à ce que votre barbe ait repoussé, puis revenez. »
fr.R: Quand David a appris ce qui s’était passé, il a envoyé des gens à la rencontre de ces hommes, parce qu’ils avaient très honte. Le roi leur a fait dire : « Attendez à Jéricho que votre barbe ait repoussé. Ensuite, rentrez. »

sw.L: Wakamwambia Daudi, naye akatuma kuwalaki, kwa maana watu hao walikuwa wameaibishwa sana. Mfalme akasema, "Kaeni Yeriko mpaka ndevu zenu zitakapoota, [ndipo] mrudi."
sw.B: Daudi alipoambiwa, alituma wajumbe kuwalaki, kwa sababu watu hao waliona aibu kubwa. Mfalme akasema, "Kaeni Yeriko mpaka ndevu zenu zitakapoota tena, kisha mrudi nyumbani."
sw.R: Daudi aliposikia yaliyotokea, alituma watu wakawalaki, kwa sababu waliona aibu sana. Mfalme akawaambia, "Ngojeni Yeriko mpaka ndevu zenu ziote tena. Kisha mrudi nyumbani."

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Đa-vít, và ông sai người đi đón họ, vì những người ấy bị sỉ nhục quá đỗi. Vua nói: "Hãy ở lại Giê-ri-cô cho đến khi râu các ngươi mọc lại, rồi hãy trở về."
vi.B: Khi được báo tin, Đa-vít sai sứ giả đi đón họ, vì những người ấy rất hổ thẹn. Vua nói: "Hãy ở lại Giê-ri-cô cho đến khi râu các ngươi mọc lại, rồi hãy trở về."
vi.R: Khi Đa-vít nghe chuyện đã xảy ra, ông sai người đi đón những người ấy, vì họ rất xấu hổ. Vua bảo họ: "Hãy chờ ở Giê-ri-cô cho đến khi râu các ngươi mọc lại. Rồi hãy về nhà."

ko.L: 그리고 사람들이 다윗에게 알리자, 그가 [사람을] 보내어 그들을 맞이했다. 그 사람들이 크게 모욕을 당했기 때문이다. 그리고 왕이 말했다. "너희 수염이 자랄 때까지 여리고에 머물다가 돌아오너라."
ko.B: 이 일이 다윗에게 알려지자, 그는 사람들을 보내 그들을 맞이하게 했다. 그들이 몹시 수치를 당했기 때문이다. 왕이 말했다. "수염이 다시 자랄 때까지 여리고에 머물러 있다가 돌아오너라."
ko.R: 다윗은 무슨 일이 있었는지 듣고 사람들을 보내 그들을 맞이했다. 그들이 너무나 부끄러워했기 때문이다. 왕이 그들에게 말했다. "수염이 다시 자랄 때까지 여리고에서 기다려라. 그런 다음에 돌아오너라."

decisions.choice: greatly humiliated: publicly disgraced
decisions.reason: The word describes the shame of being dishonored in front of others, not only a private feeling of embarrassment.

decisions.choice: stay in Jericho: wait out of sight on the way home
decisions.reason: Jericho lay just west of the Jordan, on the road from Ammon up to Jerusalem. By waiting there the envoys were spared being seen in the capital until they looked like themselves again. David's care for them also shows that he took the insult as his own.

decisions.choice: they told David: someone told him
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; it means simply that the news reached David.

decisions.choice: he sent messengers (Balanced); he sent people (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he sent". Balanced and Readable name the ones sent, which the verb implies.

source.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י נִבְאֲשׁ֖וּ בְּדָוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֡וֹן וַיִּשְׂכְּרוּ֩ אֶת־אֲרַ֨ם בֵּית־רְח֜וֹב וְאֶת־אֲרַ֣ם צוֹבָ֗א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י וְאֶת־מֶ֤לֶךְ מַֽעֲכָה֙ אֶ֣לֶף אִ֔ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ ט֔וֹב שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of Ammon that they had become a stench with David, and sent [the] sons of Ammon and hired Aram Beth-rehob and Aram Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and [the] king of Maacah, a thousand men, and [the] men of Tob, twelve thousand men.

en.L: And the sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves a stench to David, and the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, 20,000 foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah, 1,000 men, and the men of Tob, 12,000 men.
en.B: When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves hateful to David, they sent and hired 20,000 foot soldiers from the Arameans of Beth-rehob and of Zobah, the king of Maacah with 1,000 men, and 12,000 men from Tob.
en.R: The Ammonites knew that they had made David their enemy. So they paid the Arameans of Beth-rehob and Zobah to send 20,000 soldiers who fought on foot. They also hired the king of Maacah with 1,000 men, and 12,000 men from Tob.

es.L: Y vieron los hijos de Amón que se habían hecho odiosos a David, y enviaron los hijos de Amón y tomaron a sueldo a los arameos de Bet-rehob y a los arameos de Soba, 20 000 hombres de a pie, y al rey de Maaca, 1000 hombres, y a los hombres de Tob, 12 000 hombres.
es.B: Cuando los amonitas vieron que se habían ganado el odio de David, mandaron a contratar a 20 000 soldados de a pie de los arameos de Bet-rehob y de Soba, al rey de Maaca con 1000 hombres y a 12 000 hombres de Tob.
es.R: Los amonitas sabían que se habían convertido en enemigos de David. Así que les pagaron a los arameos de Bet-rehob y de Soba para que enviaran 20 000 soldados de a pie. También contrataron al rey de Maaca con 1000 hombres, y a 12 000 hombres de Tob.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Ammon virent qu’ils s’étaient rendus odieux à David, et les fils d’Ammon envoyèrent prendre à leur solde les Araméens de Beth-Rehob et les Araméens de Soba, 20 000 fantassins, et le roi de Maaka, 1 000 hommes, et les hommes de Tob, 12 000 hommes.
fr.B: Quand les Ammonites virent qu’ils s’étaient rendus odieux à David, ils envoyèrent prendre à leur solde 20 000 fantassins chez les Araméens de Beth-Rehob et de Soba, le roi de Maaka avec 1 000 hommes, et 12 000 hommes de Tob.
fr.R: Les Ammonites ont compris qu’ils avaient fait de David leur ennemi. Alors ils ont payé les Araméens de Beth-Rehob et de Soba pour qu’ils leur envoient 20 000 soldats à pied. Ils ont aussi pris à leur solde le roi de Maaka avec 1 000 hommes, et 12 000 hommes de Tob.

sw.L: Wana wa Amoni wakaona kwamba wamejifanya kuwa uvundo kwa Daudi, nao wana wa Amoni wakatuma wakawaajiri Waaramu wa Beth-rehobu na Waaramu wa Soba, askari wa miguu 20,000, na mfalme wa Maaka, watu 1,000, na watu wa Tobu, watu 12,000.
sw.B: Waamoni walipoona kwamba wamejifanya kuwa chukizo kwa Daudi, walituma watu wakaajiri askari wa miguu 20,000 kutoka kwa Waaramu wa Beth-rehobu na wa Soba, mfalme wa Maaka pamoja na watu 1,000, na watu 12,000 kutoka Tobu.
sw.R: Waamoni walijua kwamba wamemfanya Daudi kuwa adui yao. Basi wakawalipa Waaramu wa Beth-rehobu na wa Soba wawapelekee askari 20,000 wa kupigana kwa miguu. Wakamwajiri pia mfalme wa Maaka pamoja na watu 1,000, na watu 12,000 kutoka Tobu.

vi.L: Con cháu Am-môn thấy mình đã trở nên đáng ghê tởm đối với Đa-vít, thì con cháu Am-môn sai người đi thuê người A-ram ở Bết-Rê-hóp và người A-ram ở Xô-ba, 20.000 bộ binh, vua Ma-a-ca với 1.000 người, và người Tóp, 12.000 người.
vi.B: Khi người Am-môn thấy mình đã trở thành kẻ thù đáng ghét của Đa-vít, họ sai người đi thuê 20.000 bộ binh của người A-ram ở Bết-Rê-hóp và ở Xô-ba, vua Ma-a-ca với 1.000 quân, và 12.000 quân từ Tóp.
vi.R: Người Am-môn biết mình đã khiến Đa-vít trở thành kẻ thù. Vì vậy họ trả tiền cho người A-ram ở Bết-Rê-hóp và Xô-ba để gửi đến 20.000 bộ binh. Họ cũng thuê vua Ma-a-ca với 1.000 quân, và 12.000 quân từ Tóp.

ko.L: 그리고 암몬 자손이 자기들이 다윗에게 악취가 되었다는 것을 보았다. 그래서 암몬 자손이 [사람을] 보내어 벧르홉의 아람 사람들과 소바의 아람 사람들에게서 보병 20,000명을, 마아가 왕에게서 1,000명을, 돕 사람들 가운데서 12,000명을 고용했다.
ko.B: 암몬 사람들은 자기들이 다윗에게 미움을 사게 된 것을 알았다. 그래서 그들은 사람을 보내 벧르홉과 소바의 아람 사람들에게서 보병 20,000명을, 마아가 왕에게서 1,000명을, 돕에서 12,000명을 고용했다.
ko.R: 암몬 사람들은 자기들이 다윗을 원수로 만들었다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그들은 벧르홉과 소바의 아람 사람들에게 돈을 주고 걸어서 싸우는 군인 20,000명을 보내게 했다. 그들은 또 마아가 왕과 그의 군인 1,000명, 그리고 돕에서 12,000명을 고용했다.

decisions.choice: made themselves a stench to David: turned David into an enemy
decisions.reason: To become a bad smell to someone is to become hateful to him (Genesis 34:30; 1 Samuel 13:4; 27:12). The Ammonites knew war would follow.

decisions.choice: the Arameans and their neighbors: small kingdoms north and east of Israel
decisions.reason: Aram was the land of the Arameans, the region of modern Syria. Beth-rehob lay in the north near Dan (Judges 18:28; Numbers 13:21); Zobah was the kingdom of Hadadezer (8:3); Maacah lay near the Golan, east of the upper Jordan (Deuteronomy 3:14; Joshua 13:13); Tob was east of the Jordan, the land where Jephthah once lived (Judges 11:3, 5).

decisions.choice: the men of Tob
decisions.reason: The two words read most naturally as "men of Tob", the people of that land, as in verse 8. They have also been read as one man's name, "Ishtob".

decisions.choice: the parallel account in 1 Chronicles 19:6-7 gives different details
decisions.reason: Chronicles says the Ammonites paid a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim (Mesopotamia), Aram-maacah and Zobah: 32,000 chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his people, who camped before Medeba. Samuel counts foot soldiers and names Beth-rehob and Tob instead. The two writers drew on different records or counted the forces differently, and some figures may have suffered in copying.

decisions.choice: made themselves hateful to David (Balanced); made David their enemy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the picture of a bad smell. Literal keeps it.
Numbers larger than ninety-nine are written as numerals at every level.

decisions.choice: ils s'étaient rendus odieux (every level)
alternatives: ils étaient devenus en mauvaise odeur auprès de David
decisions.reason: The Hebrew picture of a stench (m1) reads oddly in French; "odieux" says its meaning plainly, and French has no common image that keeps the smell.

decisions.choice: "se habían hecho odiosos a David" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew picture is a bad smell; Spanish "hediondos" would read oddly at Literal, so Literal says "odiosos", which keeps the sense of becoming offensive to someone.

decisions.choice: "đáng ghê tởm đối với Đa-vít" (L); "kẻ thù đáng ghét" (B); "khiến Đa-vít trở thành kẻ thù" (R)
decisions.reason: Turned David into an enemy (meaning decision); Literal keeps the idea of disgust without the smell, which in Vietnamese would not read as enmity.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶת־יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־הַצָּבָ֖א הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard David, and he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.

en.L: And David heard, and he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
en.B: When David heard about this, he sent out Joab with the whole army of warriors.
en.R: When David heard about this, he sent out Joab with the whole army of fighting men.

es.L: Y lo oyó David, y envió a Joab y a todo el ejército, los valientes.
es.B: Cuando David se enteró, envió a Joab con todo el ejército de guerreros.
es.R: Cuando David se enteró, envió a Joab con todo el ejército de soldados.

fr.L: Et David [l’]apprit, et il envoya Joab et toute l’armée, les vaillants.
fr.B: Quand David l’apprit, il envoya Joab avec toute l’armée des guerriers.
fr.R: Quand David l’a appris, il a envoyé Joab avec toute l’armée des combattants.

sw.L: Daudi akasikia, akamtuma Yoabu na jeshi lote, mashujaa.
sw.B: Daudi aliposikia habari hiyo, alimtuma Yoabu pamoja na jeshi lote la mashujaa.
sw.R: Daudi aliposikia habari hiyo, alimtuma Yoabu pamoja na jeshi lote la wapiganaji.

vi.L: Đa-vít nghe [tin ấy], thì sai Giô-áp cùng toàn quân, là các dũng sĩ.
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít nghe tin ấy, ông sai Giô-áp dẫn toàn quân gồm các chiến binh ra trận.
vi.R: Khi Đa-vít nghe tin ấy, ông sai Giô-áp dẫn toàn quân gồm các chiến sĩ ra trận.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 [그것을] 듣고, 요압과 모든 군대, 곧 용사들을 보냈다.
ko.B: 다윗은 이 소식을 듣고 요압과 용사들로 이루어진 온 군대를 보냈다.
ko.R: 다윗은 이 소식을 듣고 요압에게 싸움 잘하는 군인들로 이루어진 온 군대를 주어 보냈다.

decisions.choice: all the army, the mighty men: the whole army, all of them warriors
alternatives: the whole army and the mighty men (David's elite band)
decisions.reason: The two phrases stand side by side with no "and". They are read here as one group, the army described as fighting men; 1 Chronicles 19:8 has the same words. They may also name two groups, the army and David's band of elite warriors (23:8-39).

decisions.choice: Joab: commander of David's army
decisions.reason: Joab was the son of David's sister Zeruiah (2:18) and commanded the army (8:16).

decisions.choice: warriors (Balanced); fighting men (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means strong men proven in battle. Literal keeps the traditional "mighty men".

source.text: וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַאֲרַ֨ם צוֹבָ֤א וּרְחוֹב֙ וְאִֽישׁ־ט֣וֹב וּמַֽעֲכָ֔ה לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came out [the] sons of Ammon and drew up battle [at the] entrance of the gate, and Aram Zobah and Rehob and [the] men of Tob and Maacah [were] by themselves in the field.

en.L: And the sons of Ammon came out and drew up [for] battle at the entrance of the gate, and the Arameans of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah [were] by themselves in the field.
en.B: The Ammonites marched out and formed their battle line at the gateway of the city, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob, along with the men of Tob and Maacah, took a separate position in the open country.
en.R: The Ammonites marched out and got ready for battle at the gate of their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the men from Tob and Maacah took their places away from them, out in the open country.

es.L: Y salieron los hijos de Amón y se pusieron en orden de batalla a la entrada de la puerta, y los arameos de Soba y de Rehob, y los hombres de Tob y de Maaca [estaban] aparte en el campo.
es.B: Los amonitas salieron y formaron su línea de batalla a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad, mientras que los arameos de Soba y de Rehob, junto con los hombres de Tob y de Maaca, tomaron posición aparte, en campo abierto.
es.R: Los amonitas salieron y se prepararon para la batalla a la puerta de su ciudad. Los arameos de Soba y de Rehob y los hombres de Tob y de Maaca se colocaron lejos de ellos, en campo abierto.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Ammon sortirent et se rangèrent en bataille à l’entrée de la porte, et les Araméens de Soba et de Rehob, et les hommes de Tob et de Maaka, [étaient] à part dans la campagne.
fr.B: Les Ammonites sortirent et se rangèrent en ordre de bataille à l’entrée de la porte de la ville, tandis que les Araméens de Soba et de Rehob, avec les hommes de Tob et de Maaka, prirent position à part, en rase campagne.
fr.R: Les Ammonites sont sortis et se sont préparés au combat devant la porte de leur ville. Les Araméens de Soba et de Rehob et les hommes de Tob et de Maaka se sont placés plus loin, en pleine campagne.

sw.L: Wana wa Amoni wakatoka wakajipanga [kwa] vita kwenye mlango wa lango, na Waaramu wa Soba na wa Rehobu, na watu wa Tobu na Maaka, [walikuwa] peke yao uwanjani.
sw.B: Waamoni walitoka wakajipanga kwa vita kwenye lango la mji wao, huku Waaramu wa Soba na wa Rehobu, pamoja na watu wa Tobu na Maaka, wakijipanga peke yao mbugani.
sw.R: Waamoni walitoka wakajiandaa kwa vita kwenye lango la mji wao. Waaramu wa Soba na Rehobu na watu wa Tobu na Maaka walijipanga mbali nao, kule mbugani.

vi.L: Con cháu Am-môn kéo ra và dàn trận tại lối vào cổng thành, còn người A-ram ở Xô-ba và Rê-hóp, cùng người Tóp và Ma-a-ca thì ở riêng ngoài đồng.
vi.B: Người Am-môn kéo ra và dàn trận tại cổng thành, còn người A-ram ở Xô-ba và Rê-hóp, cùng với người Tóp và Ma-a-ca, thì đóng quân riêng ngoài đồng trống.
vi.R: Người Am-môn kéo ra và dàn trận tại cổng thành của họ. Người A-ram từ Xô-ba và Rê-hóp, cùng với người từ Tóp và Ma-a-ca, thì đóng quân riêng ở ngoài đồng trống.

ko.L: 그리고 암몬 자손이 나와서 성문 입구에서 전열을 갖추었고, 소바와 르홉의 아람 사람들과 돕과 마아가 사람들은 따로 들에 [있었다].
ko.B: 암몬 사람들은 나와서 성문 어귀에 전열을 갖추었고, 소바와 르홉의 아람 사람들과 돕과 마아가 사람들은 따로 들판에 진을 쳤다.
ko.R: 암몬 사람들은 나와서 자기들 성문 앞에서 싸울 준비를 했다. 소바와 르홉에서 온 아람 사람들과 돕과 마아가에서 온 사람들은 그들과 떨어져서 넓은 들판에 자리를 잡았다.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the gate: the gate of Ammon's own city
decisions.reason: The Ammonites stayed close to the walls of their city, Rabbah, where they could retreat if beaten (verse 14).

decisions.choice: by themselves in the field: as a separate force in the open country
decisions.reason: The hired Aramean troops did not stand with the Ammonites but took up a position of their own in open ground. That placed Joab's army between two enemy forces (verse 9).

decisions.choice: the parallel in 1 Chronicles 19:9 speaks only of "the kings who had come"
decisions.reason: Chronicles does not list the allies again here, but says that the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.

decisions.choice: the gateway of the city (Balanced); the gate of their city (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the gate"; Balanced and Readable say whose gate it was.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹאָ֗ב כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה מִפָּנִ֖ים וּמֵֽאָח֑וֹר וַיִּבְחַ֗ר מִכֹּל֙ בְּחוּרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ לִקְרַ֥את אֲרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Joab that was toward him [the] face of the battle from front and from behind, and he chose from all [the] chosen [men] of Israel and drew up to meet Aram.

en.L: And Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him from in front and from behind, and he chose from all the chosen [men] of Israel and drew [them] up to meet Aram.
en.B: Joab saw that the battle lines faced him both in front and behind. So he picked some of Israel's best troops and lined them up against the Arameans.
en.R: Joab saw that he would have to fight enemies in front of him and enemies behind him. So he chose the best of Israel's soldiers and put them in place to fight the Arameans.

es.L: Y vio Joab que el frente de la batalla estaba contra él por delante y por detrás, y escogió de entre todos los escogidos de Israel y [los] puso en orden contra Aram.
es.B: Joab vio que tenía líneas de batalla por delante y por detrás. Entonces escogió a algunas de las mejores tropas de Israel y las puso en formación contra los arameos.
es.R: Joab vio que tendría que luchar contra enemigos por delante y por detrás. Así que escogió a los mejores soldados de Israel y los colocó para luchar contra los arameos.

fr.L: Et Joab vit que le front de la bataille était contre lui par devant et par derrière, et il choisit parmi toute l’élite d’Israël et [la] rangea face à Aram.
fr.B: Joab vit que les lignes ennemies lui faisaient face à la fois devant et derrière. Il choisit donc une partie des meilleures troupes d’Israël et les rangea face aux Araméens.
fr.R: Joab a vu qu’il devrait combattre des ennemis devant lui et des ennemis derrière lui. Alors il a choisi les meilleurs soldats d’Israël et il les a placés pour combattre les Araméens.

sw.L: Yoabu akaona kwamba uso wa vita ulikuwa juu yake mbele na nyuma, akachagua katika wateule wote wa Israeli akawapanga kukabiliana na Aramu.
sw.B: Yoabu aliona kwamba safu za vita zinamkabili mbele na nyuma. Basi akachagua baadhi ya askari bora wa Israeli, akawapanga kukabiliana na Waaramu.
sw.R: Yoabu aliona kwamba atalazimika kupigana na adui walio mbele yake na adui walio nyuma yake. Basi akachagua askari bora wa Israeli, akawaweka tayari kupigana na Waaramu.

vi.L: Giô-áp thấy mặt trận ở phía trước và phía sau mình, thì chọn trong tất cả những người tinh nhuệ của Y-sơ-ra-ên, và dàn [họ] ra đối đầu với A-ram.
vi.B: Giô-áp thấy mình bị kẹp giữa hai mặt trận, phía trước và phía sau. Vì vậy ông chọn một số quân tinh nhuệ nhất của Y-sơ-ra-ên và dàn trận đối đầu với người A-ram.
vi.R: Giô-áp thấy mình phải đánh quân thù ở phía trước và quân thù ở phía sau. Vì vậy ông chọn những người lính giỏi nhất của Y-sơ-ra-ên và cho họ dàn trận để đánh người A-ram.

ko.L: 그리고 요압이 싸움의 앞쪽이 앞과 뒤에서 자기를 향해 있는 것을 보고, 이스라엘의 모든 뽑힌 [사람] 가운데서 뽑아 아람과 맞서 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.B: 요압은 앞뒤로 적의 전열이 자기를 향해 있는 것을 보았다. 그래서 그는 이스라엘의 정예병 가운데서 군사를 뽑아 아람 사람들과 맞서도록 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.R: 요압은 앞쪽과 뒤쪽 양쪽에서 적과 싸워야 한다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그는 이스라엘 군인 가운데 가장 뛰어난 사람들을 뽑아 아람 사람들과 싸우도록 배치했다.

decisions.choice: the face of the battle was toward him from front and behind: he was facing enemy lines on two sides
decisions.reason: "The face of the battle" is the front line of an army. Joab found the Ammonites before the city on one side and the Arameans in the open country on the other (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the chosen men of Israel
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text read "the chosen men in Israel". The traditional reading, marked in the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts and followed here, reads "of Israel"; 1 Chronicles 19:10 has "in Israel", like the written consonants here. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: he chose from all the chosen: picked troops from the best
decisions.reason: The verb "chose" and the noun "chosen men" come from the same root. Joab took the best of Israel's soldiers to face the stronger enemy himself.

decisions.choice: Aram (Literal); the Arameans (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The land's name stands for its army. Balanced and Readable name the people, as in the rest of the chapter.

source.text: וְאֵת֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם נָתַ֕ן בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of the people he gave into [the] hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew up to meet [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And the rest of the people he gave into [the] hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew [them] up to meet the sons of Ammon.
en.B: He put the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, and he lined them up against the Ammonites.
en.R: He put his brother Abishai in charge of the rest of the army. Then they were lined up to face the Ammonites.

es.L: Y el resto del pueblo lo entregó en mano de Abisai su hermano, y él [los] puso en orden contra los hijos de Amón.
es.B: Puso el resto de las tropas al mando de su hermano Abisai, y él las puso en formación contra los amonitas.
es.R: Puso a su hermano Abisai al mando del resto del ejército. Luego los colocaron frente a los amonitas.

fr.L: Et le reste du peuple, il le donna en la main d’Abishaï son frère, et il [le] rangea face aux fils d’Ammon.
fr.B: Il confia le reste des troupes au commandement de son frère Abishaï, et il les rangea face aux Ammonites.
fr.R: Il a mis son frère Abishaï à la tête du reste de l’armée. Puis on les a placés face aux Ammonites.

sw.L: Na watu waliobaki akawatia mkononi mwa Abishai ndugu yake, naye akawapanga kukabiliana na wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: Askari waliobaki aliwaweka chini ya amri ya ndugu yake Abishai, naye akawapanga kukabiliana na Waamoni.
sw.R: Akamweka ndugu yake Abishai kuwa mkuu wa jeshi lililobaki. Kisha wakapangwa kukabiliana na Waamoni.

vi.L: Phần dân còn lại ông giao vào tay A-bi-sai em mình, và dàn [họ] ra đối đầu với con cháu Am-môn.
vi.B: Ông giao số quân còn lại cho A-bi-sai em mình chỉ huy, và dàn trận đối đầu với người Am-môn.
vi.R: Ông giao cho A-bi-sai, em mình, chỉ huy phần quân còn lại. Rồi họ dàn trận đối mặt với người Am-môn.

ko.L: 그리고 남은 백성은 그의 동생 아비새의 손에 맡겼고, 그가 암몬 자손과 맞서 전열을 갖추었다.
ko.B: 그리고 나머지 군대는 자기 동생 아비새에게 맡겨, 암몬 사람들과 맞서도록 전열을 갖추게 했다.
ko.R: 요압은 자기 동생 아비새에게 나머지 군대를 맡겼다. 그리고 그들은 암몬 사람들과 맞서도록 줄지어 섰다.

decisions.choice: gave into the hand of Abishai: put under Abishai's command
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for authority and control. Abishai was Joab's brother, another son of Zeruiah (2:18).

decisions.choice: he drew them up: Joab or Abishai
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and does not name its subject. It may be Joab, who set out both lines, or Abishai, who now commanded the second. 1 Chronicles 19:11 has "they drew up".

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word "people" here means the fighting men in the field.

decisions.choice: Then they were lined up
decisions.reason: Readable keeps open who gave the order, as the Hebrew does, by not naming the one who lined them up.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִם־תֶּחֱזַ֤ק אֲרָם֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְהָיִ֥תָה לִּ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה וְאִם־בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ יֶחֱזְק֣וּ מִמְּךָ֔ וְהָלַכְתִּ֖י לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַֽ לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, If is too strong Aram for me, then you will be for me for help; and if [the] sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to help you.

en.L: And he said, "If Aram is too strong for me, then you shall be a help to me; and if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to help you.
en.B: Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, you must come to my rescue. But if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come and rescue you.
en.R: Joab told Abishai, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come and help you.

es.L: Y dijo: «Si Aram es más fuerte que yo, tú me serás de ayuda; y si los hijos de Amón son más fuertes que tú, yo iré a ayudarte.
es.B: Joab dijo: «Si los arameos son demasiado fuertes para mí, tú vendrás a rescatarme. Pero si los amonitas son demasiado fuertes para ti, yo iré a rescatarte.
es.R: Joab le dijo a Abisai: «Si los arameos son demasiado fuertes para mí, ven a ayudarme. Si los amonitas son demasiado fuertes para ti, yo iré a ayudarte.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Si Aram est plus fort que moi, tu me viendras en aide ; et si les fils d’Ammon sont plus forts que toi, j’irai te secourir.
fr.B: Joab dit : « Si les Araméens sont plus forts que moi, tu viendras à mon secours. Mais si les Ammonites sont plus forts que toi, j’irai te secourir.
fr.R: Joab a dit à Abishaï : « Si les Araméens sont trop forts pour moi, viens m’aider. Si les Ammonites sont trop forts pour toi, j’irai t’aider.

sw.L: Akasema, "Ikiwa Aramu watanizidi nguvu, basi utakuwa msaada kwangu; na ikiwa wana wa Amoni watakuzidi nguvu, basi nitakuja kukusaidia.
sw.B: Yoabu akasema, "Ikiwa Waaramu watanizidi nguvu, lazima uje kuniokoa. Lakini ikiwa Waamoni watakuzidi nguvu, nitakuja kukuokoa.
sw.R: Yoabu akamwambia Abishai, "Ikiwa Waaramu watanizidi nguvu, njoo unisaidie. Ikiwa Waamoni watakuzidi nguvu, nitakuja kukusaidia.

vi.L: Ông nói: "Nếu A-ram mạnh hơn anh, thì em sẽ là sự giúp đỡ cho anh; còn nếu con cháu Am-môn mạnh hơn em, thì anh sẽ đến giúp em.
vi.B: Giô-áp nói: "Nếu quân A-ram mạnh hơn anh, em phải đến cứu anh. Còn nếu quân Am-môn mạnh hơn em, anh sẽ đến cứu em.
vi.R: Giô-áp bảo A-bi-sai: "Nếu quân A-ram mạnh hơn anh, em hãy đến giúp anh. Nếu quân Am-môn mạnh hơn em, anh sẽ đến giúp em.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "만일 아람이 나보다 강하면 네가 나에게 도움이 되어라. 그리고 만일 암몬 자손이 너보다 강하면 내가 가서 너를 돕겠다.
ko.B: 요압이 말했다. "아람 사람들이 나보다 강하면 네가 와서 나를 구해 다오. 그러나 암몬 사람들이 너보다 강하면 내가 가서 너를 구해 주겠다.
ko.R: 요압이 아비새에게 말했다. "아람 사람들이 나보다 강하면 와서 나를 도와라. 암몬 사람들이 너보다 강하면 내가 가서 너를 돕겠다.

decisions.choice: help, to help: rescue in battle
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb both come from the root that means to save or deliver. Here they mean coming to the aid of a fellow commander who is being overpowered, not salvation in a spiritual sense.

decisions.choice: too strong for me: stronger than the force I have
decisions.reason: The verb means "be strong"; with "for me" it means to be stronger than someone, to overpower him. Each brother promises to come to the other's side if his part of the battle goes badly.

decisions.choice: Joab said (Balanced); Joab told Abishai (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said". Balanced names the speaker, and Readable also names the one he spoke to, since the words are addressed to Abishai.

decisions.choice: help (Literal, Readable); rescue (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "rescue" to keep the strength of the word; Literal and Readable say "help". Since the word here means aid in battle, "salvation" or "save" would mislead.

decisions.choice: Joab says "anh" for himself and "em" to Abishai
decisions.reason: Brothers, as the Genesis note sets: the older (Joab, named first among Zeruiah's sons) says "anh" and calls the younger "em".

decisions.choice: Joab speaks to his younger brother Abishai in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note: an older brother speaks 해라체 to a younger one.

source.text: חֲזַ֤ק וְנִתְחַזַּק֙ בְּעַד־עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for [the] cities of our God; and Yahweh will do the good in his eyes.

en.L: Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do what is good in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes."
en.B: Be strong! Let us show courage for the sake of our people and the cities of our God. And may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do what seems good to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Be brave! Let us fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. And may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thinks is best."

es.L: Esfuérzate, y esforcémonos por nuestro pueblo y por las ciudades de nuestro Dios; y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga lo que es bueno a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos».
es.B: ¡Sé fuerte! Mostremos valor por nuestro pueblo y por las ciudades de nuestro Dios. Y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} parezca bien».
es.R: ¡Sé valiente! Luchemos con fuerza para proteger a nuestro pueblo y las ciudades de nuestro Dios. Y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crea que es mejor».

fr.L: Sois fort, et montrons-nous forts pour notre peuple et pour les villes de notre Dieu ; et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fasse ce qui est bon à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux. »
fr.B: Sois fort ! Montrons du courage pour notre peuple et pour les villes de notre Dieu. Et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fasse ce qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} semble bon. »
fr.R: Sois courageux ! Battons-nous de toutes nos forces pour protéger notre peuple et les villes de notre Dieu. Et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fasse ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} juge le meilleur. »

sw.L: Uwe hodari, na tujionyeshe hodari kwa ajili ya watu wetu na kwa ajili ya miji ya Mungu wetu; na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na afanye lililo jema machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}."
sw.B: Uwe hodari! Tuonyeshe ujasiri kwa ajili ya watu wetu na miji ya Mungu wetu. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na afanye lile analoona kuwa jema."
sw.R: Uwe jasiri! Tupigane kwa nguvu zote kuwalinda watu wetu na miji ya Mungu wetu. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na afanye lolote analoona kuwa bora."

vi.L: Hãy mạnh mẽ, và chúng ta hãy tỏ ra mạnh mẽ vì dân ta và vì các thành của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta; còn {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ làm điều tốt trong mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Hãy mạnh mẽ lên! Chúng ta hãy can đảm vì dân ta và vì các thành của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho là tốt."
vi.R: Hãy can đảm lên! Chúng ta hãy chiến đấu hết sức để bảo vệ dân ta và các thành của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm điều gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy là tốt nhất."

ko.L: 강하여라. 우리 백성과 우리 하나님의 성읍들을 위하여 우리가 힘을 내자. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 눈에 좋은 대로 행하시기를 [바란다]."
ko.B: 힘을 내라! 우리 백성과 우리 하나님의 성읍들을 위해 용감하게 싸우자. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분 보시기에 좋은 대로 하실 것이다."
ko.R: 용감해라! 우리 백성과 우리 하나님의 성읍들을 지키려고 힘껏 싸우자. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 가장 좋다고 여기시는 대로 하실 것이다."

decisions.choice: be strong, and let us show ourselves strong: an order and a shared call
decisions.reason: Joab first tells Abishai to be strong, then joins himself to the call: "let us". The second verb means to take courage and act boldly.

decisions.choice: the cities of our God: Israel's towns as belonging to God
decisions.reason: The towns of Israel stood in the land God had given his people. Defending them was defending what was his.

decisions.choice: may Yahweh do what is good in his eyes: a statement of trust that leaves the outcome to God
alternatives: and Yahweh will do what is good in his eyes
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish ("may Yahweh do") or as a statement ("Yahweh will do"). Either way Joab commits the result of the battle to Yahweh after doing all he can, as Eli and David say in 1 Samuel 3:18 and 2 Samuel 15:26.

decisions.choice: let us show courage (Balanced); let us fight hard (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to show strength. Balanced says it is courage; Readable, in a battle speech, says what that strength is for.

decisions.choice: what seems good to him (Balanced); whatever he thinks is best (Readable)
decisions.reason: "In his eyes" means "in his judgment". Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "còn CHÚA sẽ làm" (L); "Nguyện CHÚA làm" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew states it and leaves the outcome to God (meaning decision); Literal keeps the plain future, the other levels the wish the English gives.

source.text: וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יוֹאָ֗ב וְהָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽאֲרָ֑ם וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew near Joab and the people who [were] with him to battle against Aram, and they fled from before him.

en.L: And Joab and the people who [were] with him drew near to battle against Aram, and they fled before him.
en.B: Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and the Arameans fled from him.
en.R: Then Joab and his soldiers moved forward to attack the Arameans, and the Arameans ran away from them.

es.L: Y se acercó Joab y el pueblo que [estaba] con él para la batalla contra Aram, y huyeron delante de él.
es.B: Entonces Joab y las tropas que lo acompañaban avanzaron para luchar contra los arameos, y los arameos huyeron delante de él.
es.R: Entonces Joab y sus soldados avanzaron para atacar a los arameos, y los arameos huyeron de ellos.

fr.L: Et Joab et le peuple qui [était] avec lui s’avancèrent pour combattre Aram, et ils s’enfuirent devant lui.
fr.B: Puis Joab et les troupes qui l’accompagnaient s’avancèrent pour attaquer les Araméens, et les Araméens s’enfuirent devant lui.
fr.R: Ensuite Joab et ses soldats se sont avancés pour attaquer les Araméens, et les Araméens se sont enfuis devant eux.

sw.L: Yoabu na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye wakakaribia kupigana na Aramu, nao wakakimbia mbele yake.
sw.B: Kisha Yoabu na askari waliokuwa pamoja naye wakasonga mbele kupigana na Waaramu, na Waaramu wakamkimbia.
sw.R: Kisha Yoabu na askari wake wakasonga mbele kuwashambulia Waaramu, na Waaramu wakawakimbia.

vi.L: Giô-áp và dân ở với ông tiến lên giao chiến với A-ram, và chúng chạy trốn trước mặt ông.
vi.B: Rồi Giô-áp và quân ở với ông tiến lên đánh người A-ram, và quân A-ram bỏ chạy trước mặt ông.
vi.R: Rồi Giô-áp và binh lính của ông tiến lên tấn công người A-ram, và quân A-ram bỏ chạy.

ko.L: 그리고 요압과 그와 함께 [있는] 백성이 아람과 싸우려고 다가가자, 그들이 그 앞에서 도망쳤다.
ko.B: 요압과 그와 함께 있던 군대가 아람 사람들과 싸우려고 다가가자, 아람 사람들이 그 앞에서 도망쳤다.
ko.R: 요압과 그의 군인들이 아람 사람들을 공격하려고 나아가자, 아람 사람들은 그들 앞에서 달아났다.

decisions.choice: they fled before him: the Arameans ran from Joab
decisions.reason: "They" are the Arameans, and "him" is Joab. The hired army gave way as soon as Joab's picked troops attacked.

decisions.choice: the Arameans fled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the ones who fled, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, "people" means the fighting men.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי־נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֲבִישַׁ֔י וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֣שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב מֵעַל֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Ammon saw that had fled Aram, and they fled from before Abishai and went into the city; and returned Joab from against [the] sons of Ammon and came [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And the sons of Ammon saw that Aram had fled, and they fled before Abishai and went into the city. And Joab returned from [fighting] against the sons of Ammon and came [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: When the Ammonites saw the Arameans flee, they also fled from Abishai and withdrew into the city. Then Joab turned back from fighting the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
en.R: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran away from Abishai and went back into their city. So Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and went home to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y los hijos de Amón vieron que Aram había huido, y huyeron delante de Abisai y entraron en la ciudad. Y volvió Joab de [luchar] contra los hijos de Amón y llegó [a] Jerusalén.
es.B: Cuando los amonitas vieron que los arameos huían, ellos también huyeron de Abisai y se retiraron a la ciudad. Entonces Joab dejó de luchar contra los amonitas y regresó a Jerusalén.
es.R: Cuando los amonitas vieron que los arameos habían huido, ellos huyeron de Abisai y se metieron otra vez en su ciudad. Así que Joab dejó de luchar contra los amonitas y regresó a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Ammon virent qu’Aram s’était enfui, et ils s’enfuirent devant Abishaï et entrèrent dans la ville. Et Joab revint de [combattre] les fils d’Ammon et arriva [à] Jérusalem.
fr.B: Quand les Ammonites virent que les Araméens s’étaient enfuis, ils s’enfuirent eux aussi devant Abishaï et se retirèrent dans la ville. Alors Joab cessa le combat contre les Ammonites et revint à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Quand les Ammonites ont vu que les Araméens s’étaient enfuis, ils se sont enfuis eux aussi devant Abishaï et ils sont rentrés dans leur ville. Alors Joab a arrêté de combattre les Ammonites et il est rentré à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Wana wa Amoni walipoona kwamba Aramu wamekimbia, wao nao wakakimbia mbele ya Abishai wakaingia mjini. Naye Yoabu akarudi kutoka [kupigana] na wana wa Amoni akafika [mpaka] Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Waamoni walipoona Waaramu wakikimbia, wao pia wakamkimbia Abishai, wakaingia mjini. Kisha Yoabu akaacha kupigana na Waamoni, akarudi Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Waamoni walipoona kwamba Waaramu wamekimbia, wao nao wakamkimbia Abishai, wakarudi ndani ya mji wao. Basi Yoabu akaacha kupigana na Waamoni, akarudi nyumbani Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Con cháu Am-môn thấy A-ram đã chạy trốn, thì cũng chạy trốn trước mặt A-bi-sai và vào thành. Giô-áp thôi [đánh] con cháu Am-môn mà trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Khi người Am-môn thấy quân A-ram bỏ chạy, họ cũng bỏ chạy trước mặt A-bi-sai và rút vào trong thành. Bấy giờ Giô-áp thôi đánh người Am-môn mà trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Khi người Am-môn thấy quân A-ram đã bỏ chạy, họ cũng chạy trốn A-bi-sai và vào trong thành. Vậy Giô-áp ngưng đánh người Am-môn và trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 암몬 자손이 아람이 도망친 것을 보고, 그들도 아비새 앞에서 도망쳐 성으로 들어갔다. 그리고 요압이 암몬 자손과 [싸우던 데서] 돌아와 예루살렘으로 왔다.
ko.B: 암몬 사람들은 아람 사람들이 도망치는 것을 보고, 그들도 아비새 앞에서 도망쳐 성 안으로 들어갔다. 그러자 요압은 암몬 사람들과 싸우기를 그치고 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.
ko.R: 암몬 사람들은 아람 사람들이 달아나는 것을 보고, 자기들도 아비새 앞에서 달아나 성 안으로 들어갔다. 그래서 요압은 암몬 사람들과 싸우기를 멈추고 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.

decisions.choice: they went into the city, and Joab returned to Jerusalem: a victory, but not yet a conquest
decisions.reason: The Ammonites were safe behind the walls of Rabbah, and Joab did not stay to besiege it. The siege came the next spring (11:1), and the city fell only later (12:26-31).

decisions.choice: returned from against the sons of Ammon: broke off the fight with them
decisions.reason: The phrase means that Joab turned back from his campaign against Ammon.

decisions.choice: fighting
decisions.reason: "From against" needs a verb in English: Literal supplies "fighting" in brackets, and Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֔ם כִּ֥י נִגַּ֖ף לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּאָסְפ֖וּ יָֽחַד׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Aram that it had been struck before Israel, and they gathered together.

en.L: And Aram saw that it had been defeated before Israel, and they gathered together.
en.B: When the Arameans saw that they had been beaten by Israel, they gathered their forces together.
en.R: The Arameans saw that Israel had beaten them. So they brought all their soldiers together again.

es.L: Y vio Aram que había sido derrotado delante de Israel, y se reunieron.
es.B: Cuando los arameos vieron que Israel los había derrotado, reunieron sus fuerzas.
es.R: Los arameos vieron que Israel los había vencido. Así que volvieron a reunir a todos sus soldados.

fr.L: Et Aram vit qu’il avait été battu devant Israël, et ils se rassemblèrent.
fr.B: Quand les Araméens virent qu’ils avaient été battus par Israël, ils rassemblèrent leurs forces.
fr.R: Les Araméens ont vu qu’Israël les avait battus. Alors ils ont de nouveau réuni tous leurs soldats.

sw.L: Aramu walipoona kwamba wameshindwa mbele ya Israeli, wakakusanyika pamoja.
sw.B: Waaramu walipoona kwamba wameshindwa na Israeli, walikusanya majeshi yao pamoja.
sw.R: Waaramu waliona kwamba Israeli wamewashinda. Basi wakawakusanya tena askari wao wote.

vi.L: A-ram thấy mình đã bị đánh bại trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, thì họ tập hợp lại với nhau.
vi.B: Khi người A-ram thấy mình đã bị Y-sơ-ra-ên đánh bại, họ tập hợp lực lượng lại.
vi.R: Người A-ram thấy Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đánh bại mình. Vì vậy họ tập hợp tất cả binh lính lại một lần nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 아람이 자기가 이스라엘 앞에서 졌다는 것을 보고, 함께 모였다.
ko.B: 아람 사람들은 자기들이 이스라엘에게 졌다는 것을 알고 다시 군대를 모았다.
ko.R: 아람 사람들은 이스라엘에게 졌다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그들은 군인들을 모두 다시 불러 모았다.

decisions.choice: defeated: struck down in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to be struck, and is used of an army routed by its enemy (1 Samuel 4:2, 10).

decisions.choice: Aram ... it ... they: the nation spoken of as one and as many
decisions.reason: The first verbs treat Aram as a single nation; "gathered" is plural, thinking of all its soldiers. The Arameans regroup for a second campaign.

decisions.choice: gathered their forces together (Balanced); brought all their soldiers together again (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was gathered, and Readable adds "again", since this is the start of a new campaign after the first defeat.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר וַיֹּצֵ֤א אֶת־אֲרָם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ חֵילָ֑ם וְשׁוֹבַ֛ךְ שַׂר־צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Hadadezer and brought out Aram which [was] from beyond the River, and they came [to] Helam, and Shobach commander of [the] army of Hadadezer [was] before them.

en.L: And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who [were] beyond the River, and they came [to] Helam; and Shobach the commander of the army of Hadadezer [was] before them.
en.B: Hadadezer sent for the Arameans who were beyond the Euphrates River and brought them out. They came to Helam, and Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, was at their head.
en.R: King Hadadezer sent messengers to bring the Arameans from the other side of the Euphrates River. They came to Helam, and Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.

es.L: Y envió Hadad-ezer e hizo salir a los arameos que [estaban] al otro lado del Río, y llegaron [a] Helam; y Sobac, jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, [iba] delante de ellos.
es.B: Hadad-ezer mandó traer a los arameos que estaban al otro lado del río Éufrates. Llegaron a Helam, y Sobac, el jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, iba al frente de ellos.
es.R: El rey Hadad-ezer envió mensajeros a traer a los arameos del otro lado del río Éufrates. Llegaron a Helam, y Sobac, el jefe del ejército de Hadad-ezer, los dirigía.

fr.L: Et Hadadézer envoya et fit sortir les Araméens qui [étaient] au-delà du Fleuve, et ils arrivèrent [à] Hélam ; et Shobak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer, [était] à leur tête.
fr.B: Hadadézer envoya chercher les Araméens qui étaient de l’autre côté de l’Euphrate. Ils arrivèrent à Hélam, avec à leur tête Shobak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer.
fr.R: Le roi Hadadézer a envoyé des messagers pour faire venir les Araméens de l’autre côté de l’Euphrate. Ils sont arrivés à Hélam, et Shobak, le chef de l’armée d’Hadadézer, les commandait.

sw.L: Hadadezeri akatuma akawatoa Waaramu [waliokuwa] ng'ambo ya Mto, wakaja [mpaka] Helamu; naye Shobaki jemadari wa jeshi la Hadadezeri [alikuwa] mbele yao.
sw.B: Hadadezeri alituma watu wakawaleta Waaramu waliokuwa ng'ambo ya mto Frati. Wakafika Helamu, naye Shobaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Hadadezeri, akawaongoza.
sw.R: Mfalme Hadadezeri alituma wajumbe kuwaleta Waaramu kutoka ng'ambo ya mto Frati. Wakafika Helamu, naye Shobaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Hadadezeri, akawaongoza.

vi.L: Ha-đa-đê-xe sai người đem người A-ram ở bên kia Sông ra, và họ đến Hê-lam; Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, đi trước họ.
vi.B: Ha-đa-đê-xe sai người đi gọi người A-ram ở bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến. Họ đến Hê-lam, có Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, dẫn đầu.
vi.R: Vua Ha-đa-đê-xe sai sứ giả đi gọi người A-ram ở bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến. Họ đến Hê-lam, và Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của Ha-đa-đê-xe, dẫn đầu họ.

ko.L: 그리고 하닷에셀이 [사람을] 보내어 강 건너편에 [있는] 아람 사람들을 불러냈고, 그들이 헬람으로 왔다. 그리고 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들 앞에 [있었다].
ko.B: 하닷에셀은 사람을 보내 유프라테스 강 건너편에 있는 아람 사람들을 불러냈다. 그들이 헬람으로 왔는데, 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들을 거느렸다.
ko.R: 하닷에셀 왕은 사람들을 보내 유프라테스 강 건너편에 사는 아람 사람들을 불러왔다. 그들은 헬람으로 왔고, 하닷에셀의 군대 사령관 소박이 그들을 이끌었다.

decisions.choice: Hadadezer: the king of Zobah of chapter 8
decisions.reason: Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, was the strongest Aramean ruler of the time (8:3-8). His troops had already been hired by Ammon (verse 6); now he calls up his allies himself. Chapter 8 sums up David's victory over him, and this chapter tells how that war began.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with no other name means the Euphrates (Genesis 31:21; Joshua 24:2). Hadadezer's power reached the Aramean peoples living on its far side (8:3).

decisions.choice: Helam: a place east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Helam is read as a place name, as in verse 17, where it has an ending meaning "to Helam". Where it lay is not known, except that David had to cross the Jordan to reach it. The same letters could also be read "their army", and the old Greek translation took verse 16 that way.

decisions.choice: the parallel in 1 Chronicles 19:16 has no Helam and spells the commander's name Shophach
decisions.reason: Chronicles says only that the Arameans came with Shophach at their head, and in verse 17 that David came "to them". The two forms of the commander's name are the same name spelled differently.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river, which the Hebrew calls simply "the River".

decisions.choice: King Hadadezer sent messengers
decisions.reason: Readable gives Hadadezer's title and says whom he sent, so the new name is clear.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗דסוַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖א חֵלָ֑אמָה וַיַּעַרְכ֤וּ אֲרָם֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Helam, and drew up Aram to meet David and fought with him.

en.L: And it was told to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. And Aram drew up to meet David, and they fought with him.
en.B: When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Arameans lined up for battle against David and fought with him.
en.R: When David heard about it, he called together all the fighting men of Israel. They crossed the Jordan River and came to Helam. The Arameans got into battle lines to face David, and they fought against him.

es.L: Y se lo informaron a David, y reunió a todo Israel y cruzó el Jordán y llegó a Helam. Y Aram se puso en orden de batalla contra David, y pelearon contra él.
es.B: Cuando se lo dijeron a David, reunió a todo Israel, cruzó el Jordán y llegó a Helam. Los arameos se pusieron en orden de batalla frente a David y pelearon contra él.
es.R: Cuando David se enteró, reunió a todos los guerreros de Israel. Cruzaron el río Jordán y llegaron a Helam. Los arameos se pusieron en formación para enfrentarse a David, y pelearon contra él.

fr.L: Et on l’annonça à David, et il rassembla tout Israël, et passa le Jourdain, et arriva à Hélam. Et Aram se rangea face à David, et ils combattirent contre lui.
fr.B: Quand on en informa David, il rassembla tout Israël, passa le Jourdain et arriva à Hélam. Les Araméens se rangèrent en bataille face à David et lui livrèrent combat.
fr.R: Quand David l’a appris, il a réuni tous les combattants d’Israël. Ils ont traversé le Jourdain et sont arrivés à Hélam. Les Araméens se sont mis en ordre de bataille face à David, et ils l’ont attaqué.

sw.L: Daudi akaambiwa, naye akawakusanya Israeli wote akavuka Yordani akafika Helamu. Aramu wakajipanga kukabiliana na Daudi wakapigana naye.
sw.B: Daudi alipoambiwa, aliwakusanya Israeli wote, akavuka Yordani, akafika Helamu. Waaramu wakajipanga kwa vita dhidi ya Daudi, wakapigana naye.
sw.R: Daudi aliposikia habari hiyo, aliwaita pamoja wapiganaji wote wa Israeli. Wakavuka mto Yordani wakafika Helamu. Waaramu wakajipanga kwa vita kukabiliana na Daudi, wakapigana naye.

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Đa-vít, thì ông tập hợp toàn thể Y-sơ-ra-ên, vượt sông Giô-đanh và đến Hê-lam. A-ram dàn trận đối đầu với Đa-vít và giao chiến với ông.
vi.B: Khi được báo tin, Đa-vít tập hợp toàn thể Y-sơ-ra-ên, vượt sông Giô-đanh và đến Hê-lam. Người A-ram dàn trận đối đầu với Đa-vít và giao chiến với ông.
vi.R: Khi Đa-vít nghe tin ấy, ông triệu tập tất cả chiến sĩ của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Họ vượt sông Giô-đanh và đến Hê-lam. Người A-ram dàn trận để đối mặt với Đa-vít, và họ giao chiến với ông.

ko.L: 그리고 [그것이] 다윗에게 알려지자, 그가 온 이스라엘을 모아 요단을 건너 헬람에 이르렀다. 그리고 아람이 다윗과 맞서 전열을 갖추고 그와 싸웠다.
ko.B: 이 소식이 다윗에게 전해지자, 그는 온 이스라엘을 모아 요단강을 건너 헬람에 이르렀다. 아람 사람들은 다윗과 맞서 전열을 갖추고 그와 싸웠다.
ko.R: 다윗은 이 소식을 듣고 이스라엘의 군인들을 모두 불러 모았다. 그들은 요단강을 건너 헬람으로 갔다. 아람 사람들은 다윗과 맞서 싸울 준비를 하고 그와 싸웠다.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole fighting force of the nation
decisions.reason: This time David calls up the full army and leads it himself, because Hadadezer has brought the whole strength of Aram against him.

decisions.choice: to Helam: the place named in verse 16
decisions.reason: The name has an ending that means "toward", which shows it is a place.

decisions.choice: all the fighting men of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who "all Israel" were in a battle story: the men who could fight.

source.text: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜ד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שְׁבַ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֨ת שׁוֹבַ֧ךְ שַׂר־צְבָא֛וֹ הִכָּ֖ה וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled Aram from before Israel, and killed David of Aram seven hundred chariot[s] and forty thousand horsemen; and Shobach commander of its army he struck, and he died there.

en.L: And Aram fled before Israel, and David killed of Aram [the men of] 700 chariots and 40,000 horsemen; and he struck Shobach the commander of its army, and he died there.
en.B: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed the crews of 700 of their chariots and 40,000 horsemen. He also struck down Shobach, the commander of their army, and he died there.
en.R: But the Arameans ran away from the Israelites. David and his army killed the men of 700 Aramean chariots and 40,000 soldiers on horseback. They also struck down Shobach, the commander of the Aramean army, and he died there on the battlefield.

es.L: Y huyó Aram delante de Israel, y mató David de Aram [a los hombres de] 700 carros y 40 000 jinetes; e hirió a Sobac, jefe de su ejército, y murió allí.
es.B: Pero los arameos huyeron delante de Israel, y David mató a las tripulaciones de 700 de sus carros y a 40 000 jinetes. También hirió a Sobac, el jefe de su ejército, y este murió allí.
es.R: Pero los arameos huyeron de los israelitas. David y su ejército mataron a los hombres de 700 carros arameos y a 40 000 soldados de a caballo. También hirieron a Sobac, el jefe del ejército arameo, y él murió allí, en el campo de batalla.

fr.L: Et Aram s’enfuit devant Israël, et David tua d’Aram [les hommes de] 700 chars et 40 000 cavaliers ; et il frappa Shobak, le chef de son armée, et il mourut là.
fr.B: Mais les Araméens s’enfuirent devant Israël, et David tua les équipages de 700 de leurs chars et 40 000 cavaliers. Il abattit aussi Shobak, le chef de leur armée, qui mourut sur place.
fr.R: Mais les Araméens se sont enfuis devant les Israélites. David et son armée ont tué les hommes de 700 chars araméens et 40 000 soldats à cheval. Ils ont aussi frappé Shobak, le chef de l’armée araméenne, et il est mort là, sur le champ de bataille.

sw.L: Aramu wakakimbia mbele ya Israeli, naye Daudi akaua katika Aramu [watu wa] magari 700 na wapanda farasi 40,000; akampiga Shobaki jemadari wa jeshi lao, naye akafa huko.
sw.B: Lakini Waaramu walikimbia mbele ya Israeli, naye Daudi akaua watu wa magari yao ya vita 700 na wapanda farasi 40,000. Akampiga pia Shobaki, mkuu wa jeshi lao, naye akafa huko.
sw.R: Lakini Waaramu waliwakimbia Waisraeli. Daudi na jeshi lake wakawaua watu wa magari 700 ya vita ya Waaramu na askari wapanda farasi 40,000. Wakampiga pia Shobaki, mkuu wa jeshi la Waaramu, naye akafa papo hapo vitani.

vi.L: A-ram chạy trốn trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và Đa-vít giết của A-ram [quân của] 700 cỗ xe và 40.000 kỵ binh; ông cũng đánh Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của họ, và người chết tại đó.
vi.B: Nhưng người A-ram bỏ chạy trước mặt Y-sơ-ra-ên, và Đa-vít giết quân lính trên 700 cỗ xe cùng 40.000 kỵ binh của họ. Ông cũng đánh hạ Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của họ, và người chết tại đó.
vi.R: Nhưng người A-ram bỏ chạy trước quân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Đa-vít và quân của ông giết quân lính trên 700 cỗ xe của A-ram và 40.000 lính cưỡi ngựa. Họ cũng đánh hạ Sô-bác, tướng chỉ huy quân đội A-ram, và người chết ngay tại chiến trường.

ko.L: 그리고 아람이 이스라엘 앞에서 도망쳤다. 그리고 다윗이 아람에서 병거 700대[의 군사]와 기병 40,000명을 죽였다. 그리고 그가 그 군대의 사령관 소박을 쳤고, 그가 거기에서 죽었다.
ko.B: 그러나 아람 사람들은 이스라엘 앞에서 도망쳤다. 다윗은 아람의 병거 700대를 탄 군사들과 기병 40,000명을 죽였다. 또 아람 군대 사령관 소박을 쳐서, 그가 거기에서 죽었다.
ko.R: 그러나 아람 사람들은 이스라엘 사람들 앞에서 달아났다. 다윗과 그의 군대는 아람의 전차 700대에 탄 군사들과 말 탄 군인 40,000명을 죽였다. 그들은 아람 군대 사령관 소박도 쳤고, 소박은 싸움터에서 죽었다.

decisions.choice: seven hundred chariots: the men who fought from them
decisions.reason: The word means chariots or chariotry. Since David "killed" them, the sense is the crews of the chariots.

decisions.choice: the parallel in 1 Chronicles 19:18 has 7,000 chariot men and 40,000 foot soldiers
decisions.reason: Samuel has seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen; Chronicles has seven thousand chariot men and forty thousand foot soldiers. Numbers were easily miscopied, and either book may have kept the original figure. The word for "thousand" may also name a military unit, as noted at Numbers 1, which would make the forces smaller.

decisions.choice: David killed: David's army, led by the king
decisions.reason: As often in battle reports, the king is named for the army he leads (8:1-5).

decisions.choice: he struck Shobach, and he died there: Shobach fell on the battlefield
decisions.reason: "Its army" is Aram's army. In 1 Chronicles 19:18 the commander is put to death, with a word that can mean either killed in the fight or executed after it.

decisions.choice: David and his army
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that David did not kill them alone.

decisions.choice: [the men of] 700 chariots (Literal); the crews of 700 chariots (Balanced); the men of 700 chariots (Readable)
decisions.reason: The levels say that the men were killed, which is what the word means here.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֨וּ כָֽל־הַמְּלָכִ֜ים עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥מוּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּֽעַבְד֑וּם וַיִּֽרְא֣וּ אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ ע֖וֹד אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And saw all the kings, servants of Hadadezer, that they had been struck before Israel, and they made peace with Israel and served them; and feared Aram to help again [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer, saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they made peace with Israel and served them. And Aram was afraid to help the sons of Ammon anymore.
en.B: All the kings who were subject to Hadadezer saw that Israel had defeated them, so they made peace with Israel and became its subjects. After this the Arameans were afraid to give the Ammonites any more help.
